newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wheat carrier grounded off Australia floated free.
newsitem.headline: Wheat carrier grounded off Australia floated free.

text.p: A Panamanian-registered bulk carrier, on charter to the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), would be inspected for damage at the weekend after becoming grounded off South Australia, the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) said on Friday.

AMSA spokesman David Gray said the 30,400 tonne Western Winner, owned by the Hong Kong-based Fortuna shipping group, was grounded on Thursday night on a reef 28 km (15 nautical miles) south-west of the port of Wallaroo.
An AWB official said the vessel was planned to carry 25,000 tonnes of wheat, to be loaded at Wallaroo and Adelaide, to the Middle East Gulf ports of Bahrain and Sharjah.

Gray said the ship, which had come from Singapore to load at Wallaroo, was floated free on Friday afternoon and would be inspected for damage to the hull on the weekend, after travelling under its own power to Wallaroo.
"The ship will not load or leave Australia until we believe it is seaworthy," he said, adding an assessment was likely on Monday.
Gray said the vessel's master had reported no structural damage and there had been no pollution, despite its carrying 1100 tonnes of fuel oil and 116 tonnes of diesel oil.
